text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock B and C after gains, then buying back and selling some holdings at losses, shows that reacting to whether a position is above my cost can lead to inconsistent decisions; I should base trades on forward-looking value.","I realized large losses on Stocks D and E only after holding through declines. I should decide in advance what would invalidate an investment and act on that evidence rather than avoid admitting a mistake.","Several months without trades did not prevent the account from falling, and frequent trading did not reliably help either. I should review the portfolio systematically and trade only when the expected benefits justify changing my holdings."]}
